description:
There's a Giant Cloud of Alcohol in Space

Near the center of our galaxy, the gas cloud Sagittarius B2 contains huge amounts of alcohol, and a molecule that smells like rum and raspberries.

Follow for daily trips through the universe. 🚀

Images: NASA, ESA, ESO and Wikimedia Commons (free licenses, credited in the video file's notes)
Narration: AI voice

#space #galaxy #science #astronomy #shorts #science

segments.text: Out in space, there's a cloud full of alcohol, bigger than our whole solar system.

visual.query: Center of the Milky Way Galaxy IV – Composite
commons: Center of the Milky Way Galaxy IV – Composite

segments.text: It's called Sagittarius B2, a giant cloud of gas and dust near the center of our galaxy.
segments.headline: Sagittarius B2

segments.text: Radio telescopes found ethyl alcohol in it. The same kind that's in drinks.

visual.query: ALMA and the centre of the Milky Way
commons: ALMA and the centre of the Milky Way

segments.headline: Real alcohol

segments.text: And there's an unbelievable amount of it, far more than all the drinks ever made on Earth.
In 2009, astronomers also found ethyl formate there. On Earth, it gives raspberries their flavor, and it smells like rum.
But don't book a flight. It's about twenty-six thousand light-years away, and the alcohol is spread very, very thin.
segments.headline: 26,000 light-years away
